demonstrated_gap: The winners leave OCR, inferred layouts, arbitrary filings and MarkItDown's PDF/Office extras unqualified. Poppler acceptance covers only designed born-digital Latin pages. MinerU 4.0 (4.0.0 released 2026-09-16, 4.0.7 on 2026-09-23) is a local-first agent CLI. It parses PDFs, scans, DOC/DOCX, PPT/PPTX, XLS/XLSX, HTML/MHTML, EPUB and CSV in four tiers (flash, basic, standard, advanced) and keeps a local document library with `mineru find`/`search`. `mineru read` returns stable citation locators (doc:{id}/tier/page/block) plus page or block images, so an agent can re-read the original page or block before relying on a hit. That is this layer's read-the-original contract, which qmd+Poppler meets only for text. Default install: ONNX CPU small models plus a llama.cpp VLM. mineru[full] targets NVIDIA, and the default package is already the recommended one on macOS. Documents go remote only with an explicit --remote, and a local failure never falls back to remote. Measured: MinerU2.5-Pro-2605-1.2B (Apache-2.0 weights) scores 95.75 on OmniDocBench v1.6, a benchmark authored by the same lab (bias flagged). A competitor-run olmOCR-bench gives the MinerU pipeline 72.7 overall and 83.3 on born-digital pages. Flags: the code license is Apache-2.0 plus extra terms (a commercial licence is needed above 100M MAU or USD 20M monthly revenue; online services must give attribution; the licence terminates automatically on breach). Telemetry uploads stop only when explicitly disabled. The library needs a `mineru server` process to be managed. Patches ship at a high rate (8 releases in 8 days), so any trial pins an exact patch.
comparison_that_would_overturn: Build a sealed corpus with hand-checked ground truth and judged queries: born-digital filings and exhibits, difficult-layout decks and tables, scanned pages and Office files. Compare MinerU basic and standard tiers (telemetry off, no --remote, mineru[full] on the RTX 4090; macOS default package on the M5 Pro) with Poppler pdftotext for PDFs and MarkItDown 0.1.8 for HTML/Office. Measure text edit distance, table TEDS, reading-order edit and exact-phrase locator round-trip to the original page. Measure `mineru search`+`read` against qmd lex/hybrid on recall@5 and nDCG@10, with repeated cold and warm latency. Adopt MinerU as the difficult-layout/OCR parser only if it materially reduces errors on non-born-digital pages without regressing born-digital exactness or locator round-trips. Reject it if gains are within run-to-run variance.

demonstrated_gap: qmd retrieves only over extracted text. Pages whose evidence is in charts, image tables or scans (earnings decks, annual-report tables) have little or no text layer, so BM25 and text vectors cannot reach them. The layer's open gaps state that representative-corpus recall is unestablished and OCR and inferred layouts are unqualified. ViDoRe V3 (arXiv 2601.08620, revised 2026-04-21) reports that visual retrievers outperform textual ones, and that late-interaction models and textual reranking substantially improve retrieval. It includes a human-judged financial split, vidore/vidore_v3_finance_en (CC-BY-4.0). colpali-engine v0.3.18 (2026-08-22, MIT) runs Apache-2.0 ColQwen3 checkpoints locally on CUDA or MPS. tomoro-colqwen3-embed-4b (base Qwen3-VL-4B, Apache-2.0) scores 90.6 and colqwen3.5-4.5B-v3 90.9 in the README's ViDoRe table. The retrieved unit is the original page image, which can be paired with Poppler text of the same page to meet the read-original contract. The vidore-benchmark pipeline evaluator accepts arbitrary custom pipelines, so the same judged queries can score qmd's text pipeline too. That supplies part of the relevance-judged corpus the layer's next_action asks for.
comparison_that_would_overturn: Use the vidore-benchmark pipeline evaluator (custom BasePipeline) on vidore_v3_finance_en (English) plus our own sealed difficult-page subset. Compare (a) the dataset's page text, or Poppler text, fed to qmd lex and hybrid; (b) ColQwen3-4B through colpali-engine; (c) RRF fusion of (a) and (b). Measure nDCG@10 and recall@5 plus indexing and search time on the RTX 4090, with an MPS run on the M5 Pro. Adopt visual or fused retrieval as a complement to qmd only if it beats the text pipeline by a material margin on both the public finance split and our subset at acceptable index cost. Otherwise keep text-only qmd.

demonstrated_gap: PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 is the highest-ranked document parser on OmniDocBench v1.6 with both code and weights under Apache-2.0: 96.34 overall. It ranks above MinerU2.5-Pro (95.75) on a benchmark authored by MinerU's own lab. The model has 0.9B parameters (HF weights created 2026-05-27) and fits the RTX 4090 easily. It targets the OCR and complex-table gap that Poppler leaves unqualified. It is not targeted now for four reasons. It is a parser only, with no library, locator or search layer. It needs PaddlePaddle or vLLM serving. The main branch shows 4 default-branch commits since 2026-06-27 (last release v3.7.0 on 2026-06-11; HPD-Parsing announced 2026-07-22). A macOS path for the VL model is unverified; PP-OCRv6 publishes Apple M4 numbers only. Its measured edge over MinerU2.5-Pro is 0.6 points.
comparison_that_would_overturn: Run PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 on the RTX 4090 over the same sealed difficult-page subset used for the MinerU trial. Promote it to targeted if it beats MinerU's best local tier on table TEDS and text edit distance by more than run-to-run variance, at acceptable per-page latency, with block bboxes that map back to the original page.

demonstrated_gap: MarkItDown's PDF/Office extras are unestablished. opendataloader-bench is run by the opendataloader project, which is neither docling nor Microsoft. It scores markitdown 0.589 overall (tables 0.273, headings 0.000) against docling 0.882 (tables 0.887, headings 0.824). Docling (MIT, v2.130.0 on 2026-09-22, 326 default-branch commits in 90 days) runs locally, including air-gapped. It converts PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, HTML, EPUB, images and XBRL into a DoclingDocument with lossless JSON export. It also offers an MCP server and an optional GraniteDocling VLM. That makes it the clean-licence comparator for MarkItDown on non-HTML inputs. Against it: a competitor-run olmOCR-bench scores its default pipeline at 50.3. The GitHub Advisory Database lists 11 docling and docling-core advisories (8 published 2026-06-03, all fixed by 2.94.0; a docling-core RCE through unsafe PyYAML was fixed in 2.48.4). That points to a broad backend attack surface.
comparison_that_would_overturn: On the sealed corpus's Office/PDF subset, compare docling (pinned at or above 2.94.0, unneeded backends disabled) with markitdown[all] 0.1.8, the MinerU flash tier, and Poppler for PDFs. Measure text edit distance, table TEDS, heading F1, page/bbox provenance round-trip and per-document latency. Replace MarkItDown for non-HTML inputs only if docling wins materially.

demonstrated_gap: No gap is demonstrated; it is rejected. kotaemon is a Gradio chat-with-your-documents application. It delegates parsing to other loaders: its latest commit, 2026-05-30, added PaddleOCR loaders. It needs an LLM provider for answers, and a 2026-03-28 commit set a Cohere hosted reranker as the default. It publishes no retained retrieval benchmark. The default branch has no commits since 2026-05-30; v0.12.0 was released 2026-05-31. Decisive reason: it is an end-user RAG UI that duplicates qmd retrieval with a heavier, LLM-dependent stack, and development has stalled. The parsers it wraps (PaddleOCR, docling) are assessed directly above.
comparison_that_would_overturn: Maintenance resumes and a reproducible retrieval evaluation shows better recall and nDCG than qmd lex/hybrid on a judged document corpus, through a headless CLI or MCP path that works without the UI and without hosted rerankers.

demonstrated_gap: The supported successor recommended by ColPali upstream offers direct page-image retrieval for charts and layouts that text extraction can lose, plus late-interaction text retrieval. It is a plausible QMD complement, provided results resolve to the original file/body. Financial retrieval gains remain unproven.
comparison_that_would_overturn: Compare QMD's four modes with a visual side index using ColQwen2.5-v0.2 and a small late-interaction text control. Start with single-page batches on the 4090; measure smaller models on Macs. Require at least five percentage points higher Recall@5 with a positive paired confidence interval, acceptable repeated latency and 100% source-file resolution. Verify package and checkpoint licenses before installation.
evidence: [Verified v6.0.0 release](https://github.com/huggingface/sentence-transformers/releases/tag/v6.0.0) introduces MultiVectorEncoder, native package installation, page-image retrieval and bounded-memory scoring. The release was retrieved, but its status as the latest release was not established.

[Release comparisons](https://github.com/huggingface/sentence-transformers/releases/tag/v6.0.0) report LateOn versus DenseOn mean NanoBEIR scores of 0.6868 versus 0.6764, but worse FiQA2018 scores of 0.5871 versus 0.6491. This directly cautions against assuming financial-domain superiority.

[Visual-model comparison](https://github.com/huggingface/sentence-transformers/releases/tag/v6.0.0) lists ColQwen2.5-v0.2 and newer challengers including EVIE-Preview-4.5B; it explicitly warns that small benchmark results cannot replace evaluation on the user's data. Newer checkpoint licenses were not independently checked.

[ColPali migration guidance](https://github.com/illuin-tech/colpali) recommends Sentence Transformers v6 and identifies ColQwen2.5-v0.2 as Apache-2.0, while original ColPali checkpoints use Gemma terms.

demonstrated_gap: context-hub, the curated-developer-docs winner, keeps its curated content as Markdown in its own repository. That repository has no default-branch commits since 2026-06-27 (last push 2026-05-31; last release v0.1.4 on 2026-04-27), so its curated docs are not being refreshed upstream, and coverage is limited to what its registry authors choose. docs-mcp-server ('Grounded Docs', MIT, v3.2.0 on 2026-09-21) builds a private, local, version-specific index from official docs sites, GitHub repositories, local folders and zip archives. It is CLI-first, ships Agent Skills, and exposes an MCP endpoint. Search is full-text by default; embeddings are optional and Ollama is supported, so no credentials are needed. It also probes llms.txt. North-star docs (NautilusTrader 2.0, IBKR, Alpaca SDKs) could be grounded from their primary sources rather than a third-party registry. Flags: it documents telemetry, it needs Node/npx plus Playwright for hash-routed sites, and no measured quality comparison exists.
comparison_that_would_overturn: Take a fixed set of north-star documentation questions (NautilusTrader 2.0 API, IBKR adapter configuration, Alpaca SDK calls). Compare context-hub against docs-mcp-server in both FTS-only and Ollama-embedding modes: rate of correct hits from current-version primary sources, tokens returned per answer, and staleness of what is returned. Adopt only if it answers materially more questions from current primary sources at equal or lower token cost.
